A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same work, with readable text, equations, figures, and Appendices A–H. Pages 2–27 are textually and visually identical; page 1 differs only in an affiliation marker and the arXiv stamp.

before.justification: v1 reports original RFM and neural-network experiments on modular arithmetic, including accuracy, loss, feature analyses, and supplementary experiments in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experimental results in Sections 3–4 and the appendix figures.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, AGOP updates, kernel and neural-network models, and circulant-feature procedures are identical, including their appendix descriptions.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same modular addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, and simultaneous polynomial tasks, with unchanged moduli and test scenarios.

E2.justification: Figures 4 and 7 retain the same comparisons involving random circulant features. The enforced-structure and regularization comparisons in Appendix Figures 2 and 5 also retain identical comparator sets.

E3.justification: Training fractions, evaluation metrics, training budgets, model configurations, and optimization settings are unchanged throughout the main text and Appendix B.

E4.justification: Feature-reordering analyses, circulant-structure interventions, multitask grokking, regularization comparisons, and training-fraction sensitivity analyses are retained unchanged, including Appendix Figures 1–6.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Uncertainty reporting is unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical passages, plotted results, and findings match. For example, Figure 6 retains NFM–square-root-AGOP correlations of 0.955, 0.942, 0.924, and 0.929 for addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Theorem 5.1, Lemmas G.1–G.2 and proofs, and Appendix H low-rank constructions are identical.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusions retain identical claims about non-neural grokking, feature learning, AGOP, and connections to the Fourier Multiplication Algorithm.

C2.justification: Interpretations and qualifications are unchanged, including the a posteriori nature of progress measures, differences between the theorem construction and RFM, and limitations concerning model-size emergence.

D1.justification: Appendix B’s implementation, hyperparameter, and hardware information is identical. The first-page code link and its embedded target are also unchanged.

R1.justification: All 46 references and the discussion positioning the work relative to prior AGOP, grokking, and emergence research are unchanged.

P1.justification: Neil Mallinar’s affiliation marker changes from 1 to 1,2, adding the Broad Institute alongside UC San Diego. The arXiv version/date stamp is updated; prose and document structure are otherwise identical.

P2.justification: Figures 1–8, Appendix Figures 1–6, and Algorithm 1 retain identical displays, captions, and placements. No figures or tables are added, removed, or rearranged.

improvement.justification: The affiliation addition and version/date update do not meaningfully alter paper quality. Scientific content, experimental evidence, proofs, reproducibility information, and substantive presentation remain identical across the main text and appendices.
